purpose: Deterministic, transparent risk and migration methodology for the canonical CryptoAsset contract (docs/api_contract.md). Defines Mosca-style reasoning, configurable planning horizon, risk-factor guidance, scoring rules, M3 operation mapping and the governance boundary for Members 5 and 6.
principles: No quantum arrival dates are asserted or required anywhere in this project.
Timeline inputs are configurable parameters; outputs are recomputed when parameters change.
Mosca-style reasoning combines data lifetime (X), migration time (Y) and a planning horizon (Z).
Every risk factor, weight, threshold and template is defined here and in crypto_knowledge.json. Member 5 implements; it never invents.
Member 6 may format or validate this data; Member 6 does not invent classifications.

X_data_lifetime_years.meaning: How many years the protected data (or signature validity) must remain confidential or unforgeable.

Y_migration_time_years.meaning: Estimated years needed to complete a cryptographic migration for this asset.

Z_planning_horizon_years.meaning: Assumed years until a cryptanalytically relevant quantum computer threatens classical cryptography. This is an assumption, never a prediction.

planning_horizon_years.description: Organisational planning horizon used in place of an unknowable quantum arrival date. It is a scenario knob, not a fact. Dashboards must display the horizon value in use.

urgency_rule.description: An asset is exposed on the Mosca timeline when its required data lifetime exceeds the sum of migration time and the planning horizon.
urgency_rule.harvest_now_decrypt_later_precondition: Applies primarily to asymmetric encryption and key establishment where an adversary can capture ciphertext or key-agreement transcripts today and decrypt them after the quantum transition.
urgency_rule.no_dates_policy: This model never supplies Z from observable fact; Z is always the configured planning horizon. Run sensitivity scenarios at multiple horizons rather than assuming a single forecast.

risk_factors.label: Quantum-vulnerable algorithm
risk_factors.description: The primitive is vulnerable to Shor's algorithm (asymmetric: RSA, ECC, ECDSA, ECDH).
risk_factors.evaluation: Set true when crypto_knowledge.json algorithm entry has quantum_concern.shor_vulnerable == true.
risk_factors.score_delta_note: Already reflected in base_risk_score; kept as a reporting flag.

risk_factors.label: Classically broken crypto
risk_factors.description: The primitive is already broken or catastrophically weak classically (MD5, SHA-1, DES, 3DES, RSA-1024).
risk_factors.evaluation: Set true when legacy_status == BROKEN or DEPRECATED (or key_size rules flag a broken size).
risk_factors.score_delta_note: Already reflected in base_risk_score; kept as a reporting flag.

risk_factors.label: Harvest-now, decrypt-later (HNDL)
risk_factors.description: Data exposed to interception today that a future quantum computer could decrypt.
risk_factors.evaluation: Set true when the algorithm is asymmetric (encryption or key establishment) AND data is captured in transit or at rest by an adversary, AND the Mosca exposure condition (X > Y + Z) holds or data_lifetime is long.

risk_factors.label: Data lifetime exceeds horizon
risk_factors.description: Required confidentiality/integrity lifetime is longer than migration time plus planning horizon.
risk_factors.evaluation: Set true when asset.data_lifetime_years > migration_time_years + planning_horizon_years.

risk_factors.label: Internet exposure
risk_factors.description: The asset or its communications are reachable over the internet, increasing capture probability.

risk_factors.label: Signature longevity / retroactive forgery
risk_factors.description: Signatures must remain verifiable for a long period; a future Shor-enabled forgery would retroactively invalidate trust in past signatures.
risk_factors.evaluation: Set true for digital_signature assets where signed artifacts must remain verifiable for many years (certificates, firmware, long-lived documents, code-signing).

formula.step_2_key_size: adjusted = base_risk_score + key_size_adjustments[algorithm_family][key_size] (nearest defined size; unknown size adds 0.0).
formula.step_3_factors: risk_score = adjusted + sum(risk_factors[factor].score_delta for each true factor).

algorithm_resolution.key_size_source: asset.key_size; families with key_size_adjustments: RSA, ECC/ECDSA/ECDH, AES.

promotions.effect: promote one tier (e.g. HIGH -> URGENT), capped at URGENT
priority is at least HIGH, capped at URGENT

mosca_assessment_templates.broken_classical: {algorithm} is classically broken ({detail}); replace immediately - quantum is not the primary driver.
mosca_assessment_templates.hndl: {algorithm} key establishment/encryption exposes harvest-now-decrypt-later risk; data lifetime X={x} exceeds migration time Y={y} + planning horizon Z={z} under the configured horizon.
mosca_assessment_templates.transitional: {algorithm} is classically sound but Shor-vulnerable; schedule post-quantum migration within the planning horizon.
mosca_assessment_templates.signature_longevity: {algorithm} digital signatures must remain verifiable for {x} years; post-quantum forgery is retroactive - prefer ML-DSA or hash-based signatures for long-lived signed artifacts.
mosca_assessment_templates.pqc: {algorithm} is a NIST-standardised post-quantum primitive; no quantum-driven migration required.
mosca_assessment_templates.keep: {algorithm} is quantum-resilient at current parameters; no quantum-driven change required.

m3_operation_mapping.description: Maps the operation strings the source scanner emits (Member 3, detectors/*.py) onto the canonical primitives defined in crypto_knowledge.json. Member 5 resolves an asset's effective primitive jointly from (algorithm, operation).

encryption.family_hint: resolved from algorithm id; default symmetric
encryption.note: Java Cipher and JS createCipher are used for both symmetric and asymmetric; classify by algorithm.

decryption.family_hint: resolved from algorithm id; default symmetric

keyexchange.note: Legacy vocabulary alias used in early API-contract examples; normalise to key_establishment.

randomness.note: SecureRandom, os.urandom, secrets, randomBytes, subtle.generateKey non-key uses.

crypto_import.note: Bare crypto library import; weak signal.

m3_mapping_review.summary: Review of Member 3 source scanner output against this knowledge base and the canonical contract.

findings.findings: Operation vocabulary is inconsistent across detectors: Java emits 'encryption', Python emits 'symmetric_encryption'; key agreement is 'key_agreement' while the API contract example used 'keyexchange'; hashing is 'hashing' in code but 'hash' in contract examples.
findings.remediation: Normalise through m3_operation_mapping in this file. Canonical primitives live in crypto_knowledge.json.operation. Update the M3 detectors to emit canonical tokens or rely on this mapping.

findings.findings: 3DES is emitted as 'DESede' (java detector) and 3DES/DES-EDE3 elsewhere; resolved to the 3DES entry via aliases in crypto_knowledge.json.
findings.remediation: No change required; aliases already cover DESede, 3DES, DES-EDE3, DESEDE.

findings.findings: No post-quantum detection: ML-KEM and ML-DSA are not in any detector's known-algorithm list, so PQC-positive codebases are invisible.
findings.remediation: Add ML-KEM-{512,768,1024} and ML-DSA-{44,65,87} to the Java/JS/Python known-algorithm lists and library docs.

findings.findings: key_size is left null by detectors (java.py never extracts sizes; javascript.py sometimes encodes size in the algorithm string, e.g. aes-256-gcm). Key-size adjustments in this methodology cannot apply without key_size or an embedded size.
findings.remediation: Extract numeric sizes from algorithm strings (e.g. allow AES/2048 patterns) and set asset.key_size. For encoded forms, the alias table captures the default key size in the notes.

findings.findings: Bare 'EC' / curve names (secp256r1, P-256) surface without a primitive. Java Signature.getInstance("SHA256withECDSA") is already resolved as ECDSA, but KeyAgreement EC findings need operation context.
findings.remediation: Resolve 'EC' and curve names through the ECC entry; the primitive is decided by operation (KeyAgreement -> ECDH, Signature -> ECDSA). Documented in crypto_knowledge.json ECC notes.

findings.findings: algorithm may be null (bare imports, os.urandom, heuristics). The knowledge base provides fallback_rules keyed by operation so Member 5 can still score deterministically with review_required true.
findings.remediation: No change required; risk engine must honour review_required and surface these for human confirmation.

findings.findings: Java Cipher.getInstance lines are deduplicated by 'keep longest api' heuristic (java.py lines 101-106); a single line can produce only one finding, potentially dropping a second distinct primitive.
findings.remediation: Document in scanner README; accept as a known limitation or emit one finding per distinct algorithm on the line.

m5_methodology_review.summary: Member 5 (risk engine) does not yet exist as a module in this repository. This section reviews the persistence contract the risk engine must implement and the risk fields it will populate.

findings.findings: The canonical CryptoAsset schema reserves risk_score, risk_level, migration_priority, mosca_assessment and recommendation as nullable fields, populated by the risk engine; RiskAssessment carries an optional factors dict.
findings.remediation: Member 5 must compute these fields using this file (scores, thresholds, priority promotions, templates) and crypto_knowledge.json (base scores, resolution). The factor keys emitted in RiskAssessment.factors must match risk_factors[].id.

findings.findings: If Member 5 hard-codes its own weights, thresholds or algorithm table, results diverge from this methodology and Member 6 cannot render a consistent view.
findings.remediation: Load methodology.json, crypto_knowledge.json and recommendations.json at startup; treat them as read-only reference data. Unit-test score determinism against the fixtures in tests/test_crypto_knowledge.py.

findings.findings: The 'risk_score' float is unbounded in the Risk schema (ge 0, le 10), matching the 0..10 scale here.
findings.remediation: Keep the clamp in risk_score_definition.step_4_clamp; do not widen the range.

findings.findings: Mosca assessment is a free-form string in the contract, so its content is at Member 5's discretion.
findings.remediation: Prefer mosca_assessment_templates so output stays consistent; include the planning_horizon_years value used in the narrative so the assumption is transparent.

findings.findings: business_criticality is a Member 3 input and is intentionally OUTSIDE the risk-score formula, keeping crypto-risk signal independent of business labelling.
findings.remediation: Keep business_criticality as a visible column; it may inform reporting order but must not silently change risk_score.

governance.m6_constraints: Member 6 may format, validate and render this data and the other Member 2 JSON files. Member 6 must not invent algorithms, families, legacy statuses, risk factors, weights, thresholds or priority tiers. Any UI classification label must trace to this file or crypto_knowledge.json.
governance.sensitivity_guidance: Run exposure at multiple planning horizons (e.g. default, min, max) and surface HNDL assets whose data_lifetime_years is within the horizon buffer.
